match.reason: Neither bank point teaches government infrastructure investment as a budgetary supply-side policy that lowers business costs and raises capacity: the climate change point is about climate damage to the economy, and the LRAS point is about aggregate supply theory.

draft.title: Infrastructure
card: Infrastructure is the physical and digital networks that an economy runs on, such as roads, rail, ports, airports and broadband. Governments often fund it, and private firms sometimes build or run it.
Better infrastructure cuts business costs. Faster freight and reliable networks mean less time lost and lower transport costs for each unit of output.
It also raises the economy's capacity, or the most it can produce. Firms can reach more workers, suppliers and customers, and can produce more with the same resources.
Because it works by cutting costs and lifting capacity, infrastructure spending is a budgetary aggregate supply policy. It takes years to build, so the gains come over the long term.
draft.remember: Infrastructure cuts business costs and lifts capacity, so it shifts supply over the long term.

a.q: How does a new freight rail line to a port help to lift the economy's capacity?
opts: It lowers transport costs, so firms can make and sell more
It raises workers' skills, so each hour of work yields more
It gives firms grants to develop new products and methods
It lowers the tax that firms pay on each unit they sell
a.why: A freight line cuts the time and cost of moving goods, so firms can reach more markets and produce more. Training lifts skills and research grants support new methods, but those belong to other supply policies and are not how a rail line works.
a.clue: Think about what a rail line changes for a firm moving goods.

b.q: The Victorian Government funds a new broadband network for regional towns. Which result best shows how this raises the economy's capacity?
opts: Regional firms reach more customers and produce more
Households spend more as the network project hires workers
Regional firms pay less tax on the profits that they earn
Regional schools run more courses to lift workers' skills
b.why: Better broadband cuts costs and lets firms reach more customers and produce more, which lifts capacity. Hiring workers to build the network adds to spending for a time, but that is a short-term demand effect and does not raise what the economy can produce.
b.clue: Which result lasts after the network is built and changes what firms can produce?

a.best: It lowers transport costs, so firms can make and sell more

b.best: Regional firms reach more customers and produce more
